newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index wipes early losses, ends 1.16 pct up.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index wipes early losses, ends 1.16 pct up.

text.p: Bombay blue chips staged a late rally to finish at the day's highest levels on Thursday, on the back of speculative short-covering and gradually-rising optimism that the market's downside risk was limited, traders said.

"It (buying) is largely speculative short-covering, but we are still not seeing the level of foreign institutional buying needed to prop up the market," said Neeraj Roy, head of institutional sales at Prime Broking.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) rallied 42.83 points, or 1.16 percent, to end at 3,731.90 after tumbling nearly three percent on Wednesday.
The Bombay index surged nearly 16 percent to an eight-month high of 4,029.56 in early March, from a close of 3,474.79 on February 28, the day the budget was announced.

"Just after the budget, a lot of people built speculative positions on the hope that foreign institutional investors would jump on the bandwagon," said Sridhar Narayan, investment analyst at mutual fund ITC Threadneedle.

But, the index tumbled nearly seven percent and traders say foreign funds are maintaining a low profile. The budget proposals slashed corporate and personal taxes, raised foreign portfolio limit in firms and allowed firms to buy back shares.
"We need prices to stablise. I think the index should move between 3,650-3,750 over the next 5-10 days," said Ashith Kampani, head of deailing at JM Share & Stock Brokers.
"Lots of money should flow in once we see some stability in the market," Kampani added.

Shares of Nestle India climbed five rupees to close at 223.0 rupees at the Bombay bourse after the company announced a 27 percent jump in 1996 net profit to 528 million rupees against 416 million rupees in the year-ago period.
